newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Russia to discuss Afghanistan, nuclear deal.
newsitem.headline: India, Russia to discuss Afghanistan, nuclear deal.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda will visit Moscow next week for talks with Russian President Boris Yeltsin, including an exchange of views on Afghanistan, a spokesman said on Thursday.
The two leaders will also review the proposed sale of Russian nuclear reactors to India, a deal the United States wants Moscow to scrap, he said.

Diplomatic sources said the visit could also result in a meeting between Foreign Minister Inder Gujral, a member of the Indian team on the four-day visit starting on Monday, and his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen due in Moscow at the same time.
Gujral told Reuters on Wednesday he had no immediate plans to meet Qian in Moscow "but I would definitely like to meet my colleague if there is an opportunity".
The Indian and Chinese ministers are expected to be briefed by Russian officials on Yeltsin's summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton beginning in Helsinki on Thursday, diplomats said.
Both countries share Russia's opposition to NATO's expansion plans in Eastern Europe.

"On Afghanistan, we share Russia's concerns on the rising tide of religious fundamentalism," an Indian foreign ministry official told Reuters. "We believe the rise of Islamic Taleban in Afghanistan has also upset the Central Asian countries."

Asked if Moscow planned to call off the nuclear reactors offer to India following U.S. pressure, the Indian spokesman said: "Our understanding is that Russia does not allow third parties to influence its decisions in such matters."
The New York Times quoted U.S. officials last month as opposing the planned sale of two light-water nuclear reactors to India, saying it violated an international agreement.
The newspaper quoted an unidentified senior U.S. official as saying the sale would be a setback for worldwide efforts to stop the spread of nuclear weapons.
The official also said the "Russian Federation, as signatories to the 1992 suppliers' agreement, should not be selling these controlled nuclear technologies".

The suppliers' agreement forbids suppliers from exporting nuclear technology to aspiring nuclear powers. Sales are forbidden to countries not formally recognised as nuclear weapons states and which do not allow international inspections of key nuclear institutes.
Only the U.S., Russia, Britain, France and China are recognised nuclear weapons states.
Russian officials insisted the sale to India should be exempt from the agreement because it was included in an earlier understanding between then-President Mikhail Gorbachev and Indian leaders.
The initial agreement to build the reactors was reached in 1987.
Russian officials say the value of the sale to India was $1.5 billion to $2 billion for each of the light-water reactors.
India exploded an atomic device in 1974 but says its atomic programme is peaceful.
